Commentary.Commentary: India have a crucial 56-run lead and with the pitch taking vicious turn, the home side can run away with the show with sensible batting and draw the curtains on the visiting side. Stay tuned for India's reply...

Terrific turnaround from India! The duo of Ashwin and Jadeja were terrific and ran through the lower order of the Kiwi side in a jiffy. Armoured with venomous turners and arm balls, they bamboozled the batsmen completely and toppled them like a pack of cards. Jadeja took a fifer and Ashwin scalped four wickets to wrap up the visiting side for 262. New Zealand were poor today in their application and once the century stand between Williamson and Latham was broken, it was a processing with the lower half not contributing much.

Ashwin in his follow through has to dive to his right to grab an excellent catch. Watling who was looking for some quick runs to decrease the lead has to depart. NEW ZEALAND ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 262!

Ronchi and Santner showed good application and stitched together a 49-run partnership before the former was a bit unlucky to be adjudged LBW. Watling is looking unsettled out there and it won't be a surprise if the Indian bowlers run through the lower order of the visiting side. Will the Kiwi batsmen put up a brave show and fight back? Join us for the post lunch session to find out!

Ashwin and Jadeja have done the bulk of the bowling as expected and have been exceptional. They have let the ball do the talking as it has turned viciously and the roughs have helped both of them to extract extra bounce off the track. Ashwin troubled Latham and outwitted him with a clever delivery. That opened the floodgates as a couple of more wickets fell in quick succession. Taylor went for a duck as he fell to Jadeja and it needed a magical delivery by Ashwin to send Williamson packing.

That marks the end of second day's play between India and New Zealand. The day belonged to the Kiwis as they bowled out India within the first half hour of the day and gave a solid reply with the bat piling up 152 runs for the loss of just one wicket. The Indian bowlers were disciplined and varied their lines and lengths intelligently but were unlucky to only get a single breakthrough! Tom Latham and Kane Williamson batted with grit, determination and courage to put New Zealand in a strong position.
The news out from the middle is that PLAY HAS BEEN CALLED OFF. Rain has officially spoilt the day!

UPDATE 1525 IST - There's some positive news as the rain has stopped pouring down. The groundstaff are already on it and trying to dry up the water on the field. Slowly the covers are being peeled off. The umpires will make their next inspection at 1545 IST. We'll keep you guys posted.

UPDATE 1445 IST - Rain is not even hinting of slowing down and the ground remains fully covered. Whereas the light has gone from bad to worse. The chances of seeing some cricketing action late in the day seems slimmer and slimmer.

UPDATE 1430 IST - Sadly folks, the rain doesn't seem to slow down and the whole of Green Park is covered with covers. Even the floodlights have been turned on so the bad light may come into play later on. Stay tuned as we keep updating you!
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

As we were heading for the tea break, the groundsmen came running in with the covers as the rain caught up the speed and started coming down heavily. Hope it goes away soon and we get to complete the last session of the day's play. So stay tuned for further updates!

The Indian bowlers bowled decent lines and created some hiccups to both the Kiwi batsmen but were unable to get the breakthrough. If things like a dropped chance by Rahul at short leg and an unlucky caught behind decision against Williamson had gone their way, the tide might have turned.

New Zealand has claimed another session under their name. The pair of Latham and Williamson saw it through completing their respective half centuries. They played with calmness and confidence, sweeping the spinners, using their feet against them and putting the bad balls away whenever required.

Earlier in the session, India came onto bat and added 27 runs to their overnight total before Wagner took the wicket. New Zealand will now want Williamson and Latham, who look settled to play a long innings as they have the patience to play it. Kohli would want his bowlers as well as his fielders to step up their performances. Let's see what the second session has in store for us...

Good session for the Kiwis! They just had one loss in Martin Guptill, who fell to Umesh Yadav after an aggressive start. After that, Tom Latham with his skipper Kane Williamson saw off the rest of the session without much hiccups. The Indian bowlers bowled decently with Yadav being the only successful bowler. The disappointment for the home side will be the bowling of Ashwin, who looked unsettled in the middle due to the clever batting by the tourists' skipper. India showed a poor effort in the field with more than a couple of misfields leaking away some runs.
